# Response types

What each method returns, as recorded from FortiAIGate 8.0.2. Every type is a
`TypedDict` (import it from `pyfortiaigate` to annotate your own code); at
runtime every record is a plain `dict`. All fields are optional: a field the
appliance leaves out is absent, so read with `.get()` when in doubt.

The [Actions](../actions.md) page shows which method returns which type.
Calls that could not be verified live (org-level writes such as `invite`, and
ICAP logs) are untyped `JSON`.

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from src/pyfortiaigate/client.py; do not edit. -->

## Argument types

Aliases used in method signatures.

| Name | Is | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| [](){#pyfortiaigate.client.WsRef}`WsRef` | `str \| Mapping` | A workspace: its id, its name, or its record |
| [](){#pyfortiaigate.client.Ref}`Ref` | `str \| Mapping` | A detector, guardrail, policy or key: id, name or record (a key also by its `faig_...` secret) |
| [](){#pyfortiaigate.client.Day}`Day` | `date \| str` | A report date: a `date` or `"YYYY-MM-DD"` |
| [](){#pyfortiaigate.client.When}`When` | `datetime \| int` | A log time: a `datetime` (naive = UTC) or epoch milliseconds |
| [](){#pyfortiaigate.client.JSON}`JSON` | `Any` | An untyped response: the decoded JSON as-is |
